question.text: If the solution of the differential equation <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi></math> (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is an arbitrary constant), then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
The given equation is
dx2y=sin⁡xdx
On integrating, we get, 
x2y=-cos⁡x+C

or x2y+cos⁡x=C
⇒k=2
